name: DocSend
tagline: Share pitch decks and documents as tracked links instead of attachments, with page-by-page view analytics and access controls.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The mechanics here are not exotic: convert a PDF to page images, serve them behind a token URL, log which page was on screen and for how long. An agent can get that working end to end, including an email gate, link expiry, passcode and a per-visit timeline, in a weekend. What it cannot manufacture is the social fact that a docsend.com link reads as normal to an investor while a link on your own domain reads as a curiosity, or worse, as something a spam filter should eat. You also inherit every ugly edge: fonts that render wrong, huge decks, mobile pinch-zoom, someone screenshotting anyway. Fine for tracking who actually read your deck, weaker as the thing you paste into a cold intro.
coreLoopDIY: Upload a PDF, get a tokenized viewer link with optional email gate and expiry, and see per-visitor per-page dwell time in a dashboard.
requirements: Node 20 and a small always-on host with a domain and TLS
Object storage or plain disk for uploaded PDFs and rendered page images
Poppler (pdftoppm) or pdfjs-dist available for server-side page rendering
Optional SMTP credentials if you want the email gate to actually verify addresses
whatYouLose: The brand signal: recipients recognize a DocSend link and open it without thinking
Data rooms, folder-level permissions and multi-document deal spaces
Click-through NDA and e-signature flows that hold up in a real diligence process
Serious deterrents against download and copying, plus the audit trail that goes with them
CRM and email integrations, mobile-tuned viewer, and someone else fixing the PDF that renders wrong
moatNotes: The product is a tracked PDF viewer. The pricing power comes from being the tracked PDF viewer that fundraising culture already agreed on.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the link goes to someone whose time you are asking for, and any friction is your fault. A DocSend link is invisible infrastructure to a VC: they click, it renders, they move on. Your self-hosted viewer on deck.yourname.dev invites a half-second of suspicion, and in fundraising or sales that half-second is real. Add the diligence-grade stuff, per-document permissions, NDA gates, an audit log a lawyer will accept, and the DIY version stops being a weekend project.
notes: The tracking is easy, the trust is not. Build it for internal docs and client proposals, keep paying when the reader is a stranger with money.
prompt:
Build a self-hosted document sharing app with per-page view analytics, like a personal DocSend.

Stack, no substitutions: Next.js 15 (App Router, TypeScript), Tailwind, SQLite via better-sqlite3, files on local disk under ./storage. No auth provider, no analytics SDK, no telemetry, no cloud services.

Owner side (single user, gated by ADMIN_PASSWORD from .env, cookie session):
- Upload a PDF. On upload, render every page to a PNG at ~1400px wide using pdftoppm (shell out) and store page count in SQLite.
- Create one or more share links per document. Each link is a random 22-char token and has settings: require email before viewing (yes/no), optional passcode, optional expiry timestamp, allow download (yes/no), active (yes/no).
- Dashboard listing documents, then per-link visits: timestamp, email if captured, IP-derived country if trivially available (else blank), total seconds, pages reached, and a small bar chart of seconds per page.
- Ability to deactivate a link instantly.

Viewer side (public, no account):
- GET /v/[token] validates active/expiry, then shows passcode form or email form if configured, then the viewer.
- Viewer renders page images in a vertical scroll container, lazy loaded, plus prev/next and a page counter. No pdf.js on the client, images only.
- Client tracks which page occupies the most of the viewport and accumulates dwell time per page, flushing batched events to POST /api/track every 5 seconds and on visibilitychange/pagehide via sendBeacon.
- If allow download is off, do not expose the original PDF at any route; only serve page images. Add a light watermark of the viewer email on each served image if an email was captured (server-side composite is fine, or CSS overlay if you prefer, say which you chose in the README).

Explicitly out of scope: data rooms, folders, NDA or e-signature, multi-user teams, CRM integrations, email sending (store the submitted email unverified and note this in the README), screenshot prevention.

Deliverables: working app, schema created on first run, seed script that ingests a sample PDF, .env.example with ADMIN_PASSWORD, and a README covering pdftoppm install, backup of ./storage plus the SQLite file, and one honest paragraph on what this does not stop a determined viewer from doing.
